page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. The server does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong compute and memory capabilities. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng benchmarks and strong multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth is strong for large block reads at 329.44 GB/sec and writes at 143.42 GB/sec. The hardware supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI, which assist in cryptographic and mathematical operations. In LLM inference tests, the NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier performance for smaller models with 3898.64 tokens/sec for prompt processing, while maintaining strong to average speeds for medium and large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high-density resource profile combining a modern enterprise GPU with a substantial memory footprint, making it suitable for specialized workloads without the overhead of dedicated physical infrastructure. However, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant load. The lack of local storage is another key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science, LLM serving, and memory-intensive analytical processing.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated and memory-intensive workloads. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 192.0 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. The CPU operates on the x86_64 architecture with a shared allocation model, delivering top-tier single-core performance and strong multi-core capabilities. While the server lacks local storage, its memory bandwidth and vector instruction support are highly rated. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in small-model LLM inference and strong results in database operations and decompression tasks. This configuration is optimized for machine learning inference, data science, and analytical workloads requiring significant GPU acceleration and memory capacity.
